question: Since its creation in 2016, the EU Trust Fund for Colombia has been a flexible and effective tool for promoting peace, democracy and human rights.

As stated in written question E-002261/20231 about funding mechanisms to support the strengthening of Colombian communities, the end of this mechanism is a concern for Colombian civil society and victims of conflict who understand how it could hamper progress in the implementation of the 2016 Final Peace Agreement and in talks and negotiations with the armed groups National Liberation Army (ELN) and Central General Command (EMC).

Some Member States, as well as the EU itself, are participating in these negotiations as guarantors and partners. How does the Commission plan to contribute financially to peacekeeping in Colombia when the fund comes to an end?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (26.4.2024) The EU is fully committed to supporting the peace process in Colombia and the implementation of the 2016 Peace Agreement. Through its support, the EU has become a privileged partner and a trusted and reliable interlocutor for national and international stakeholders in this process.

Between 2016 and 2022, the EU invested approximately EUR 220 million supporting peacebuilding, including through the EU Trust Fund (EUTF, EUR 130 million), and the bilateral envelope for Colombia. The EUTF has been an effective instrument to leverage financial contributions and political participation, especially from Member States.

However, as all EU trust funds will be discontinued under the present Multiannual Financial Framework, the Commission is working on options to maintain a consistent level of support to the peace process and political engagement during the 2021-27 programming period. The multiannual indicative programme for 2021-2024 allocates EUR 27.

9 million to continue supporting peace in Colombia in the framework of a Team Europe Initiative, with a multi-sector perspective and in cooperation with Member States. The Foreign Policy Instruments complement this support, including the project on ‘Support to peace consolidation in Colombia’ (EUR 2.5 million).

To leverage additional EU support, the Commission is also exploring blended finance, guarantees, regional and thematic programmes. Sustainable finance, in particular climate and biodiversity-linked instruments, will be crucial to scale up EU support. The objective is also to connect relevant Global Gateway initiatives, e.g. on connectivity, with building peace and State presence in conflict-affected territories.
